findings.title: Access-token matcher does not verify the expected grant
findings.body: The grant occupies indexes 4–5 of the six-character prefix, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5) and rejects equality instead of inequality. Consequently, an ID such as `onrtna:<uuid>` passes an assertion expecting the authorization-code grant `ac`. This leaves the updated authorization-code, refresh, device, and CIBA assertions unable to detect missing or incorrect grant encoding. Check the prefix length and reject when substring(4, 6) does not equal the expected shortcut.

findings.title: Enforce the shortcut width required by the token format
findings.body: Grant shortcuts are accepted without a length check, while the decoder requires exactly six context characters and reads exactly two characters for the grant. The new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory contract even describes a typical shortcut as three letters. A custom grant following that contract can therefore start successfully and issue tokens whose IDs cannot be decoded by this same provider. Document the two-character requirement and validate it when registering shortcuts, including the lazy registration paths, so unsupported shortcuts cannot produce unreadable token IDs.
